answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing escrowed jobs that counterparties later confirm; opening an account grants no weight. A new identity must therefore fund real work and persuade independent partners to accept and verify it before it can shape prices or allocate tasks. Sybils cannot multiply voting power for free: the attacker pays deposits, labor, and transaction fees across identities, while risking disputes and lost escrow. They may wander from one oasis of cheap jobs to another, but each route up the knoll still requires costly, verifiable exchange.
